## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Hevatthikathā* ("Debate on 'It Exists Thus'") is the tenth discourse of the first chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The debate centers on the proposition that phenomena exist only in a specific manner (*evatthi* / *hevatthi*) and not otherwise [Dube 1980]. According to modern scholarship, this controversy addresses a thesis attributed to the Andhakas (including the Pubbaseliyas) holding that the past, present, and future exist strictly as past, present, and future respectively, rather than otherwise [Dube 1980]. The Theravādins criticize this formulation on the grounds that it inadvertently predicates both existence and non-existence to the same phenomenon [Dube 1980]. The dialectical exchange contrasting *hevatthi* and *hevanatthi* against the Theravādin positions (*sevatthi* and *sevanatthi*) has been noted for its formal resemblance to the Jain doctrine of conditional predication (*saptabhaṅgīnaya*) [Dube 1980].

**Sources**
